title: Judgment on Judah's Gloating Neighbors
overview: After Babylon destroys Jerusalem, Ezekiel announces judgment on four neighboring peoples who cheered, mocked, or took revenge during Judah's disaster.

parts.label: Ammon cheers the ruin (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: Ammon, a kingdom east of the Jordan River, said "Aha!" when Babylon defiled the temple in Jerusalem, wrecked the land and carried Judah's people into exile. In return, desert tribes from the east will move in, and the capital Rabbah (where Amman in Jordan stands today) will become a place for camels and sheep to rest.

parts.label: Clapping over a neighbor (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: Clapping hands and stamping feet meant open celebration, taking delight in a neighbor's suffering. The sentence is severe, ending Ammon as a people, and it closes with the chapter's repeated line that they will know the LORD, meaning they will learn who truly rules events.

parts.label: Moab's mockery (vv. 8-11)
parts.note: Moab and Seir (another name for Edom's homeland) sneered that Judah was no different from any other nation, as if its God had not protected it and it was nothing special after all. Moab's frontier towns, the pride of its land, will be opened up, letting the same eastern invaders in.

parts.label: Edom's revenge (vv. 12-14)
parts.note: Edom, south of the Dead Sea, had a long feud with Israel, and other passages say it joined in when Jerusalem fell and turned on fleeing survivors (Psalm 137, Obadiah). The whole country is to be laid waste, people and animals alike, and Israel itself is named as the means of God's vengeance.

parts.label: The Philistines' old hatred (vv. 15-17)
parts.note: The Philistines on the Mediterranean coast had been Israel's enemies for centuries, and here they are accused of using that long grudge to try to destroy Judah. The Kerethites (also spelled Cherethites) were a group among them, possibly linked to Crete, and the Hebrew plays on their name, roughly "I will cut off the Cutters."

think: Why might taking pleasure in someone else's downfall feel so different from simply wanting justice to be done?
